Mr. Lincoln. Your speeches are admired, and rightly so – you have a way with words that stirs the blood of many a good Republican. But let us be candid, and this panel values candor above all else. You have lost elections before, and Douglas, for all his moral failings, is a formidable opponent. We need a candidate who can win.

Tell us, if you would, about a time your political judgment proved wrong. A position you took publicly that you now wish you hadn’t, or a campaign decision that cost you dearly. How did you handle it? What lessons did you draw from that experience that you believe would serve you, and this party, should we entrust you with this nomination?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text:
Gentlemen, I appreciate your candor and your concerns. It is true that I have faced defeats in the past, both in elections and in other endeavors. One particular instance that comes to mind is my decision to support the Kansas-Nebraska Act in 1854. At the time, I believed that allowing the residents of those territories to decide on the issue of slavery for themselves was a fair compromise. However, I soon realized the grave mistake I had made in underestimating the spread of slavery and the importance of taking a firm moral stand against it.

In the aftermath of that decision, I faced criticism and backlash from many quarters. But instead of shying away from my error, I took it upon myself to educate myself further on the issue of slavery and the principles of liberty and equality that our nation stands for. I learned that it is not enough to compromise on matters of fundamental human rights, and that sometimes, one must take a stand, even if it is unpopular.

From that experience, I have drawn the lesson that true leadership requires moral courage and a steadfast commitment to principles, even in the face of adversity. If entrusted with this nomination, I would bring that same moral clarity and unwavering dedication to the cause of justice and freedom to the Senate. I believe that our party, and our nation, deserve leaders who are willing to make the hard decisions and stand up for what is right, no matter the cost.
